source.title: Nucleotide Transformer: building and evaluating robust foundation models for human genomics
source.authors: Hugo Dalla-torre; Liam Gonzalez; Javier Mendoza-Revilla; Nicolas Lopez Carranza; Adam Henryk Grzywaczewski; Francesco Oteri; Christian Dallago; Evan Trop; B. D. de Almeida; Hassan Sirelkhatim; Guillaume Richard; Marcin J. Skwark; Karim Beguir; Marie Lopez; Thomas Pierrot

record.tranche_reason: Extends model-scaling evaluation to DNA language models and reports downstream task performance across model sizes; it does not test the original held-out loss scaling laws directly.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates downstream genomic-task scores across model sizes (Fig. 5c), which bears on V6. Fig. 5a plots training loss against training tokens, but does not report held-out loss or fit/test a power law; it is not recorded as a result for V1, V2 or V5. Other benchmark results are not extracted because they do not compare scale or loss with downstream performance.
record.test_reason: The study reports fine-tuned downstream MCC across DNA language-model sizes (Fig. 5c, Fig. 2b), a new setting for V6. Only within-family size comparisons count. No held-out loss sweep, power-law fit, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or shape ablation is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that increasing model size 'leads to consistently improved performance' on the 18 tasks. They add that data diversity and architectural and training changes let a 50M NT-v2 model match the v1 500M models, and a 250M model reach the best score (0.769).
record.recipe_differences: Masked-language modeling of six-mer DNA tokens; comparisons use downstream genomic-task MCC rather than held-out language-model loss. Models differ in pretraining data, architecture and token budgets.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream scores vary with model size, pretraining dataset, model version and number of training tokens; the paper reports that the 250M model’s improvement over the 500M model appears only after longer training.

fits_no_version.finding: Fig. 5a plots NT-v2 training loss falling with tokens seen, for four sizes, with no held-out evaluation or fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training (not held-out) MLM loss of DNA LMs decreases with training tokens and model size.

record.problems: The reported size comparisons are not controlled solely for parameter count: architecture, pretraining data and training-token budgets differ. Fig. 5c provides labeled aggregate scores without uncertainty estimates. No held-out pretraining-loss scaling fit or compute-optimal allocation test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows left out. The training-loss-versus-token plot in Fig. 5a was not extracted because it is training loss, not held-out loss, and the paper does not test a power-law fit.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining-loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute. Fig. 5a shows training loss only, with no power-law fit.
No extrapolation of fitted laws to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation study. Chinchilla is cited only as motivation for longer training.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
DNA modality, but no test of whether loss follows a power law.
No fitted or predictive scaling relation. Downstream performance is not related to pretraining loss. Only 2–4 sizes per family are compared.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Downstream MCC vs pretraining tokens for each NT-v2 size. The text states 250M overtakes 500M only after 900B tokens, implying 500M ≥ 250M before that.
missing.locator: Fig. 5b; Results 'Model optimization for cost-effective predictions'

missing.what: Per-task fine-tuned MCC by model size. The text says larger models consistently outperformed smaller counterparts.
Probing accuracy on genomic-element classification by model size (2.5B > 500M).

record.verdict_notes: Cross-family comparisons (v1 vs v2, HumanRef vs 1000G vs Multispecies) confound size with architecture, data and tokens, so R5 and R7 are unlinked. The authors' claim of 'consistent' improvement with size is contradicted by their own 250M > 500M result. No uncertainty is shown for the Fig. 5c aggregates.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss power laws in parameters, tokens or compute; no such loss sweep or fit is reported.
No prediction of larger-run held-out loss from fits on smaller runs.
No fixed-compute optimization or comparison of parameter/token allocations.
No controlled comparison of depth, width or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Although the models use DNA sequences, the paper does not test whether held-out loss follows the same power-law form; its plotted training loss is not a held-out evaluation or a power-law fit.
The paper compares downstream genomic-task performance across model sizes, but does not test its predictability from pretraining loss or fit a predictive scaling relationship.
No study of how fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with fitting choices.

relationships.condition: NT-v2 multispecies, 50M to 250M parameters (same data and architecture)
relationships.reason: Mean MCC rises 0.732→0.748→0.769 with size (R1–R3). The 50M→100M step is at equal tokens; the 250M step also has more tokens.
relationships.display_finding: Mean MCC increased from 0.732 to 0.748 to 0.769; tokens were equal at the first size increase and increased at the second.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: NT-v2 multispecies, 50M to 250M parameters (same data and architecture)
source_check.reason: R1–R3 show increasing category-aggregated MCC: 0.732, 0.748 and 0.769. The architectural recipe and dataset are shared; the 250M checkpoint also uses more tokens.

relationships.reason: 500M scores below 250M (0.762 vs 0.769, R4). The 1000G 5x size increase gains only 0.009 MCC despite 6x tokens (R6, R8). Improvement with size is not monotonic or uniform.
relationships.display_finding: NT-v2 500M scored 0.762 versus 0.769 for 250M, while a fivefold NT-v1 size increase added only 0.009 MCC despite sixfold training tokens.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R3–R4 show a lower aggregate score at 500M than at 250M; R8–R6 show only a 0.009 gain with five times the parameters and six times the tokens. These qualify the uniformity of downstream gains.

source_check.notes: The plotted values are standalone scores; the pack's proposed sequential baselines are analytical comparisons. MCC aggregates category medians rather than averaging all 18 tasks equally; these comparisons establish conditional gains, without validating quantitative scaling forecasts.
